page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.32xlarge is an enterprise-tier, memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs driven by 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processors, offering high-density parallel computing capacity without core sharing or burstable scheduling constraints.

Designed for memory-intensive architectures, the platform supplies 1024.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on networked cloud disks for operating system and application storage layers. High-throughput data transport is supported by a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. The instance does not feature GPU acceleration hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its substantial core count and 1 TB memory capacity, this instance targets large-scale, memory-bound enterprise systems. It is particularly matched for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large relational database management systems, and memory-resident big data analytics pipelines where RAM capacity and high network bandwidth are essential bottlenecks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.32xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processors on an x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization. Providing 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of system RAM, it maintains a dense 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation designed for memory-intensive execution environments. The instance includes 64 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without integrated local disk storage, directing persistent input and output operations to remote cloud storage. There are no hardware accelerators or bundled public IPv4 addresses included in the profile. The massive memory footprint and broad processing capacity make this server well suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching architectures, in-memory analytic engines, and high-concurrency enterprise transaction processing workloads.
